newsitem.title: UKRAINE: FORECAST-Ukraine PM sees 15-16 pct inflation in 97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Ukraine PM sees 15-16 pct inflation in 97.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said on Friday inflation this year could fall to 15-16 percent, much lower than a previous government forecast of 25 percent and 39.7 percent last year.

"In the parameters of the budget we are setting an inflation figure of 24.8 percent but we think it will really be 15-16 percent," Lazarenko told a meeting with local leaders in the eastern coalmining region of Donetsk.
Lazarenko also said wage arrears in Ukraine stood at 3.4 billion hryvnias at the start of May while the state owed pensioners 1.2 billion hryvnias.
The size of the mountain of unpaid wages, pensions and benefits was put at 5.5 billion hryvnias in March.
Monthly inflation was 0.8 percent in April, up from 0.1 percent the previous month. Prices grew by 4.4 percent over the first four months against 23.9 percent in the same 1996 period.
The economics ministry plans to slash a 20 percent subsidy for gas, electricity and communal services from June 1.
